observations.observation: All nine panels show transverse cross-sections of one knee/leg, including separate long-bone cross-sections and axial condylar/patellofemoral anatomy. Axial anatomy agrees with tra descriptions and axial IOP group. Anatomy appears rotated in image display, with anterior patella toward right in middle panels; no image reorientation inferred.

All three rows show recognizable sagittal anatomical knee profiles: individual rounded femoral condyle profile, bent femur/tibia relation and sagittal extensor chain/patellar profile. These appear anatomically sagittal and agree with sag descriptions, despite patient-coordinate IOP group coronal.

All three rows show recognizable coronal anatomical views, with both femoral condyles side-by-side, broad tibial plateau and central notch in middle panels; posterior/distal variations visible. These agree with cor descriptions despite patient-coordinate IOP group sagittal.

Three strongly oblique partial femoral/notch cross-sections; insufficient to assign an exact anatomical plane solely by visual inspection. Retain oblique classification, no forced coronal/sagittal reassignment.

conclusion: The six numeric description/IOP disagreements are real, but visible anatomy supports the original sagittal/coronal descriptions. Do not automatically swap sequence routing to patient-coordinate IOP classes. Limb positioning or reference-coordinate discrepancy could explain mismatch; cause not established. Need compare official Anatomical_Plane and actual dataset routing before any change.
